messages:
maria (PM): Quick sync — after yesterday's outage we need to update the PRD and RFC for Dynamic Routing v2. We missed several guardrails. Need acceptance criteria, runbook additions, and scope alignment. @sam @katie
sam (Eng): Agree. Root cause looked like cache eviction + fallback into larger model variant under burst. We should add explicit fallback thresholds in the spec and deterministic variant selection rules.
katie (SRE): From SRE: add circuit breaker per-route, per-customer token throttles, and alerts: latency P95 > 1.2s OR error rate > 0.5% for 5m triggers rollback. Also require a smoke test post-deploy.
miguel (Customer Success): Customers reported cost spikes when fallback kicked in. Need a cost-safety guardrail: if per-customer token spend > $threshold within 1h, automatically throttle to baseline model and send CS notice.
josh (Design): UX requirement: show a lightweight "degraded mode" banner with reason + ETA to users of affected routes. Acceptance: banner appears within 2s of mode flip and includes CTA to retry.
maria (PM): Drafting PRD updates now. Proposed acceptance criteria (short): 1) fallback occurrences <= 0.1% under overload test; 2) per-route latency SLO maintained for 99% traffic; 3) auto-rollback if error spike >1% sustained for 10m; 4) cost throttle + customer notification implemented.
sam (Eng): Technical reqs to capture: tie KV cache TTL to route config, bounded concurrency per model instance, deterministic model-variant mapping (no randomness), feature-flag gating for progressive rollout, and explicit metrics emitted for every fallback.
katie (SRE): Runbook additions: immediate rollback command documented, CLI to redirect traffic to warm pool, smoke test commands, and update incident template to include "model variant used" and "cache hit rate" fields.
maria (PM): Launch criteria checklist idea: docs + runbook updated, canary rollout 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%, stability window of 48h with no SLO breaches, and sign-offs from Eng, SRE, and CS.
miguel (Customer Success): I'll draft a customer comms template and a mitigation offer (small credits) for affected customers. Can get a draft by EOD.
sam (Eng): I'll add acceptance tests into the CI harness for simulated overload/fallback and assert the fallback rate and latency thresholds. Assigning to me and alex.
maria (PM): I'll open the RFC PR with the PRD diff in a few hours. Reviewers: @sam @katie @josh @miguel. Link: https://redwood.company/rfcs/dynamic-routing-v2 (placeholder).
deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: 2026-04-01T14:00:00Z (canary 1%).
katie (SRE): Add one more metric: median KV hit rate >= 70% on the caching path — helps detect cache misconfig before fallback.
sam (Eng): Good call. Will add metric and make it part of the gate.
maria (PM): One open scoping question: do we limit the initial rollout to hosted API only, or include Dedicated customers? My preference is hosted first and Dedicated only after 2 stable canaries. Thoughts?
miguel (Customer Success): For Dedicated customers with high spend, we should offer an opt-in test window. They often want more control.
josh (Design): UX changes for Dedicated dashboards need a slightly different banner that links to account rep. Keep that in the scope for Dedicated only.
sam (Eng): Technically doable but increases rollout matrix. Recommend hosted-only initial canary.
maria (PM): OK hosted-only initial. I'll reflect that in the RFC and update the rollout plan. I'll post the PRD update by 12:30 and request reviews. If no objections, we proceed with canary plan.
